pr_title: drivers: usb: dc: stm32: Added implementation to functions
pr_body:
Added the attached state to the USB stm32 driver,
and logging for when the device is not attached.
Also added implementation for the **usb_dc_detach**,
**usb_dc_reset** and **usb_dc_ep_flush** functions.
The **usb_dc_ep_flush** uses HAL_PCD_EP_Flush under the hood, that
uses the ll_usb. It doesn't return an error if a timeout occurred (T/RXFFLSH bit stays 1),
and it also doesn't check before doing flush if the core is reading/writing to the FIFOs.
The usb_dc_ep_disable should also AFAIK flush the FIFO, but the HAL_PCD_EP_Close
doesn't do it. I think that the usb_dc_ep_set_stall should also flush the TxFIFO (for IN endpoints).
The **usb_dc_reset** will return timeout, after **USB_STM32_CORE_RST_TIMEOUT_US** microseconds,
that parameter may be converted to a Kconfig configuration, or changed as needed.
Also the reference manual says we need to wait 3 PHY clock cycles, that I don't know how much that is,
and how to calculate, so I just took what I saw in another driver. Would like to be corrected here.
I ran a simple project that enables and disables the USB device, and resets it.
Checked with lsusb, and dmesg, and for enable/disable, show the events in dmesg,
but for reset didn't saw anything.
Did not check flush, but it is the same implementation of flush as in the ll drivers, just without checking for
timeout.
Are we supposed to see an event when we reset the USB device? It didn't return a timeout error, so I believe it works
I based my implementation on the reference manual, HAL's and ll's, and other drivers, but I believe there may still be things missing, so would happy to get some critique.

Closes #36211

Signed-off-by: Prema Jonathan van Win <jonathanvanwin@gmail.com>

@JonathanVanWin I've pulled in your PR and have tested the usb_dc_ep_flush() functionality.

I've added a line:

```
k_sem_give(&ep_state->write_sem);
```

To my code to allow another write to the USB EP.

I imagine thats not how it should be done. When and from which context should usb_dc_ep_flush() be called.

For context I want to cancel a transfer to the host if a timeout has been exceeded, and need to flush the endpoint so new transfers can take place.

issue_context.title: usb: stm32: not implemented functionality
issue_context.body:
**USB subsys functions use unimplemented functions in stm32 USB driver**
There are three functions that are currently not implemented in the stm32
USB driver (from the LOG's that I can see):

- **usb_dc_ep_flush**
- **usb_dc_detach**
- **usb_dc_reset**

The problem is that when you use functions such as usb_deconfig (from the USB subsys), they call the USB driver
and those will print that they are not implemented.

**Finish the USB stm32 driver implementation**
As far as I know, the other USB drivers implemented all the necessary behaviour, used by the subsys and by the driver itself,
and by looking at their own implementations, it seems that the detach and reset functions are pretty trivial.

**Started implementing those functions**
I took the ideas from the other drivers and understood that the detach needs to update the attached state (to check if attached before calling other functions), disable USB IRQs, and soft disconnect (some also disable clocks).
I tried doing this, by writing directly to the **USB_BASE_ADDRESS** + 0x804, and enable BIT(1), that is the soft disconnect;
and also disabled this bit at the end of the usb_dc_stm32_init function (tried before and after the call to irq_enable).
The problem is that the first time you call usb_enable, it works, then you call usb_disable, and it also works (using my changes),
but it seems that after that I cannot enable it again.
The reset function looks that is to clear the data struct and reset the peripheral, but didn't try it.
